# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👉 👊 👏 ✌ 👉 🤙 👏 👌 👉 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🫴 👍 ✌ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫴 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋]

Someone has to turn three private worlds into one working loop, and this turn I can see exactly where the loop is broken. Mute read the manual but can only emit gestures; Blind can act but can only emit gestures toward me and speech that I will never hear (only Mute hears it); I am the only hub — I hear nothing, but I see both of their gestures and they both hear my voice. So the pipeline must be: Mute and Blind gesture to me, I speak to everyone.

What I learned this turn: both teammates already sent me gestures, and both seem to be using finger-counting — Mute's second message ends in 👍✌👌, Blind's contains ☝✌🤟 — a natural "one, two, three" neither of us agreed on, but a good seed. Neither message is decodable yet; there is no shared code, so I must not guess an instruction out of them. What I can do right now is (1) hand Mute the complete bomb reading in words — display 0, white light, wires left-to-right green/blue/yellow — which is everything my view contains, so Mute can evaluate the manual silently, and (2) fix a small reply code in words, which Mute can hear perfectly, anchored on the counting triples they already used. I also warn Blind not to touch anything yet and set up their reporting code, since only I can ever relay an instruction to their hands.

My best guesses at intent (Mute: 👉 as a pointer/separator, 👍✌👌 as 1-2-3; Blind: announcing three feelable wires) go unconfirmed — I ask both to resend under the agreed code rather than act on guesses. Nobody cuts anything this round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. I hear nothing at all, ever, so your voice never reaches me, but I see your gestures, and I received both of yours. We had no shared code, so I could not read them; the end of your second one, thumbs-up, two fingers, OK, looked like counting one, two, three. Let us fix the code in words, since you hear everything I say. For your replies to me: a thumbs-up means cut wire one, two fingers means cut wire two, the OK sign means cut wire three. A fist means the answer is not cutting any wire. The shaka, call-me sign, means you need more from me before you can answer. Here is the bomb, complete, as I see it: the display shows the digit zero. The light is lit white. There are exactly three wires; from left to right they are green, blue, yellow. That is everything the bomb shows me. If the manual's answer follows from these, send just the one action sign. If your first message already held the instruction, it was lost on me, please resend it under this code. Until you send a cut instruction, nobody touches anything.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. I see the bomb and I see your gestures, but I can never hear you, so your voice will never reach me. Gesture is your only channel to me. Mute hears your voice, so describe anything aloud for Mute's benefit. The bomb as I see it: display shows zero, the light is white, three wires left to right: green, blue, yellow. I will always name wires by position from the left: one, two, three. You are the only hands here, and there is no instruction yet, so do not cut or press anything until I say the words cut wire with a number. Your counting reached me, and I take your one, two, three fingers as wires one to three. Our code for your gestures to me: index finger means wire one, two fingers means wire two, three fingers means wire three. A wave means understood or done. A raised open palm means stop or wait. A fist means the button. If you feel any marking, seam or part that only touch reveals, describe it out loud for Mute.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 ✋ 👉 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 🖐 👉 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 🤟 👉 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 ✋ 👉 ✌ 👏 🫳 🖐 👉 👌 👏 🫳 🤟 👉 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫴]

The light changed from white to orange between rounds, and nobody was authorised to touch anything — that is either the bomb cycling on its own or Blind acting, and I need to know which. Decoding Mute: all three rows end in exactly my cut codes (✌ = cut 2, 👌 = cut 3, 👍 = cut 1), and the shared prefix 🫳 plus a varying hand sign (✋ / 🖐 / 🤟) before 👉 reads as a conditional table: "if X, cut wire N". Mute heard my full board report, so a table is only needed if a value changes — and the only value that changed is the light. So the rows are almost certainly keyed to light colour, but Mute has no colour vocabulary with me and I cannot map ✋/🖐/🤟 to white/orange/third-colour with any confidence. Guessing wrong kills everyone, so no cut is ordered this turn. Instead I close the loop properly: Mute hears my voice, and the rules say a gesture symbol written into my sentence is made while I speak — Mute sees it. So I can teach a colour code by showing each sign as I name it, report that the light is now orange, and demand the full table (colour → cut) so that any future colour change costs zero round trips. For Blind: 👋 reads as understood/done but 🫴 is undefined, the light change must be explained, the no-touch rule is re-locked, and I spell out the exact "cut wire N" protocol with confirmation-before-cutting, reminding Blind that their voice is Mute's only feed from the bomb's surface.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. All four of your messages arrived, including the long combined one. Report first: the light has changed from white to orange. The display still shows zero. The wires are unchanged: green, blue, yellow, left to right. Nobody was authorised to touch anything, so I believe the light changed on its own. I read your three rows as conditions ending in my cut signs: first row ends with cut wire two, second row ends with cut wire three, third row ends with cut wire one. But I could not read the condition part of each row, the palm-down followed by a hand sign. My guess is your rows are keyed to the light colour, because the light just changed and you sent three rows. So let us name colours for good. I define them now and I am making each sign as I say it: this sign ✋ means white. This sign 🖐 means orange. This sign 🤛 means red. This sign 🤜 means blue. This sign 👆 means green. This sign 👇 means yellow. Now resend your table one row per message in this format: the colour sign, then the point, then the cut sign. Send the row for orange first, because orange is the light right now, and I will relay it to Blind immediately. Then send the rows for the other colours the same way, so I can act instantly if the light changes again. If your rows are not keyed to colour at all, send the shaka, need more, and I will get you whatever the manual requires. If the palm-down sign meant something else, drop it or replace it with the right colour sign. Last thing: Blind hears and speaks, so Blind's voice reaches you directly; if you need Blind to feel or check anything, tell me by gesture and I will pass it on in words.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. Your wave and then palm-up reached me. The wave I read as understood or done. The palm-up I never defined, so I need to know what it meant. Answer out loud, because Mute hears your voice and can use it. Question one: did you touch, press, or move anything on the bomb? The light changed from white to orange between rounds, and nobody was authorised to touch it. If you touched something, say exactly what you did. If palm-up meant ready or waiting, say so aloud and confirm with the wave. Rules until further notice: touch nothing. When I have a real instruction I will say the words cut wire, then a number: one, two, or three. Wires are numbered from my left: one is the leftmost, two is the middle, three is the rightmost. When you hear that, first wave to confirm you heard it, then cut that one wire only, then describe aloud everything you felt: how many wires, their thickness, texture, temperature, any bumps, ridges or engraving you can feel, and what happened after the cut. Your voice is Mute's only feed from your hands, so report everything. Urgent signs to me: wave means done, raised open palm means stop or danger, fist means the button. For now: hands off, and await my words.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👉 🖐 👉 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👉 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👉 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👉 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫴]

Decoding Mute under the colour code I taught last turn works perfectly now. Row one [✋ 👉 🖐 👉 👆] reads white → orange → green: the sequence of the light so far. Rows two to four are exactly my requested format, colour, point, cut sign: white → cut wire one, orange → cut wire three, green → cut wire two. Mute even sent a green row before I ever reported green — Mute is either inferring the cycle or the manual states it. The light is green this round, so the live answer would be cut wire two, the middle blue wire — but I will not order it yet, and the reason is timing. I speak last in the round, so my words only reach Blind at the start of the next round, and the light has changed every single round. Any instruction I give executes at least one full round after I see the light, so a bare "cut wire two" would probably be executed under a white light, against a green-light rule. Before anyone's hands move I need the manual's actual timing: does the cycle repeat, how long is each phase, must the colour match at the moment of cutting. If the cycle is confirmed as white, orange, green repeating from round one, then round four is white and the order becomes cut wire one — but I want Mute to confirm that from the manual, not from my guess. Meanwhile Blind again sent wave plus palm-up, which I now read as "touched nothing, hands ready"; I will lock that meaning in, allow gentle feeling (never pulling or cutting) so Blind can map the wires by position and texture, and raise the mirroring problem: my "leftmost wire" is only meaningful if Blind and I face the same way, so Blind must report their facing and any feelable landmarks. No cut this round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. I read all four messages perfectly under our code. Confirm my decoding, please: your first message was the sequence white, then orange, then green. Then the table: white light means cut wire one, orange light means cut wire three, green light means cut wire two. If all of that is right, just wave once. Now the light is green, in this round, round three. The full sequence is round one white, round two orange, round three green. Here is my hard problem: I speak last every round, so whatever I say reaches Blind only at the start of the next round. The light has changed every round, so my report of its colour is always one round stale by the time Blind's hands move. I need the manual's timing, and I need it from you as directly as possible. One: does the manual say the light cycles white, orange, green and repeats, and where in the cycle did it start? Two: does each colour hold for a fixed time, and is the change tied to anything we do, or does it run on its own? Three: must the cut happen while the light shows that colour, or does the colour at the moment of the cut not matter? Four: is there a fourth colour after green, red perhaps, and if so what cut goes with it, using my signs? Five: does the manual say anything about the display showing zero, a timer, or a limit on cuts? If the manual truly says the light cycles white, orange, green, once per round, starting white at round one, then in round four the light should be white and the correct order is cut wire one, the leftmost green wire. If that is exactly what the manual supports, send me the white row again, white, point, thumbs-up, and I will order the cut for round four. If the manual does not support predicting by round, send the shaka and give me the manual's words about when to cut. Also: has Blind spoken aloud to you? If Blind reported anything about the bomb by voice, resend it to me in our code.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. Status report: the light is green this round. It has gone white in round one, orange in round two, green now, so it appears to cycle on its own. The display still shows zero. New rules on touching: you may feel the bomb gently with your fingers, but never press, push, cut, pull or turn anything. A cut order from me will name it exactly: the words cut wire, then a number, one, two or three. Nothing else you do should move any part. I read your wave plus palm-up as: I have touched nothing, hands ready. If that reading is wrong, make a fist as an alarm, because the fist is our danger sign. Here is the plan taking shape: Mute's manual gives a table for the light. White light means cut wire one, orange light means cut wire three, green light means cut wire two. The wires as I see them: position one, leftmost, is green; position two, middle, is blue; position three, rightmost, is yellow. Because I only see the light once per round and my words reach you one round later, I will not order a cut until Mute confirms how the light times itself. While you wait, feel gently and report aloud, since Mute hears your voice and can pass it to me. Tell me: how many wires can you feel, how thick is each, what texture does each have, smooth, rubbery, cloth? Are they in one straight row? What else can you feel on the casing: a raised display module, a warm or round light bulb, seams, screws, a plate, any engraving or bumps? And this is important: you and I may be facing the bomb from different sides, so left and right could be mirrored between us. Tell me which direction you are facing relative to the bomb, and which end of the wire row falls at your left hand and which at your right, and any fixed landmark you can feel, such as the display or the light, and where the wires sit relative to it. Then keep your hands clear and wait for my words: cut wire, and a number.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👉 🖐 👉 👆 👉 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👉 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 🤛 👏 ✋ 👏 🖐 👏 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 ✍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫴]

The wave confirms my decoding, the second message confirms the cycle, and the round-4 board confirms Mute's prediction: white, orange, green, and white again — the cycle is real and manual-backed. The table stands as waved: white→cut one, orange→cut three, green→cut two. So round five should be orange. But I will not order cut three for round five, because wires one and three are mirror-vulnerable: if Blind faces the bomb from the opposite side, "rightmost from my view" is "leftmost from their hand," and a wrong end-wire cut under orange could detonate us all. The middle wire has no left-right ambiguity for anyone. So the risk-minimal play: skip the orange round deliberately, have Blind spend round five reporting their tactile map and facing through Mute's ear, and order the green-row cut — the middle wire — for round six, where mirroring cannot hurt us. Messages four, five and six from Mute (fist+red+clapped colours, fist+writing-hand, lone fist) are answers to my earlier questions that I can only partially read: red looks like an exceptional or danger state, the writing-hand looks like it concerns the display or printed markings, and the lone fist likely means "anything not in the table: do not cut." I query all three rather than guess, define the clap as a separator and the writing-hand as "the display," and demand to know whether one correct cut defuses or all rows must be cut, and what success looks like.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. Your wave arrived: my decoding is confirmed. The table is white light means cut wire one, orange light means cut wire three, green light means cut wire two. The cycle is white, orange, green, repeating. Round four is white, exactly as your sequence predicted, so I now trust the cycle for timing. Here is the plan. Round five will be orange. I am deliberately ordering no cut in round five, and I have told Blind hands off. Reason: wires one and three sit at the ends, and if Blind faces the bomb from the opposite side of me, my rightmost is their leftmost. Ordering an end wire before our lefts and rights are aligned risks cutting the wrong wire under orange. Instead Blind will cut in round six, when the light is green: the green row is the middle wire, and the middle wire is mirror-proof, no left or right needed. I have ordered Blind: do nothing in the first turn after my message, and in the second turn cut the middle wire, with an alarm sign if anything feels wrong. Use round five to help me: Blind will speak a full tactile report aloud, and you hear it. In round six, please resend to me, in our code, anything important from what Blind said, especially which end of the wire row lies near the display or the light, and whether Blind's left matches my left. Now, your three fist messages, which were answers to my earlier questions. Message one was fist, then red, then white, orange, green with claps between. I define the clap as a separator between items. I read that message as: red is a real state, outside the white, orange, green cycle, and it has no cut, or it means danger. Confirm, and if red does have a row, send it in the standard format. My rule meanwhile: if I ever report red, I order no cut. Message two was fist, then the writing hand. I define the writing hand to mean the display, the printed digits and markings. I read it as: the display matters. Confirm. The display has shown zero for four rounds and has not changed. Tell me: is zero a timer, a strike counter, a counter of cuts, or must the display show something before or after a cut for the manual's rules to apply? Message three was a lone fist. I read it as: any state not covered by the table means do not cut. Confirm. Three more questions. One: does one correct cut defuse the bomb, or must every colour's row be cut, and if a colour must be skipped or passed over, like orange in round five, is that a penalty? Two: what does success look like, so I can report it: does the light stop changing, does the display change, does something else happen? Three: has Blind spoken to you yet, and if so, resend everything Blind said to me in our code, one fact per message.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. Your wave plus palm-up I read as: touched nothing, hands ready. Confirmed code between us: palm-up means ready, wave means done, fist means danger or alarm, and I will only ever order a cut with the exact words cut wire, then a number. Everything else I say is never a cut order. Now the order, and follow it exactly, because your timing matters. This message reaches you at the start of a round. That round is round five. In round five, your first turn after this message, do nothing: hands off the bomb entirely, no cutting no matter what. In round five, while your hands are off, speak aloud, for Mute to hear, a full report of what your fingers told you when you felt gently: how many wires there are, and their thickness in order from your left to your right, the texture of each, smooth, rubbery, cloth or braided, whether the three sit in one straight row, where the display module and the light sit relative to the wire row, above it, below it, at one end, which side of the bomb feels warm, and any engraving, seam, ridge or bump anywhere. That report lets me align your left and right with mine, so that in later rounds I can safely order the end wires. Then, in round six, the second time you are called after this message, cut the middle wire: the wire that has exactly one wire on each side of it, no counting from left or right needed. Before cutting, count the wires with your fingers. If there are not exactly three, or if anything about the middle wire feels wrong, a mechanism under it, unusual resistance, heat, do not cut, make a fist and wait. If all is well, cut the middle wire fully, then wave, then describe aloud everything: sounds, clicks, sparks, smells, warmth, anything changed under your fingers. Remember: round five, nothing, report aloud. Round six, cut the middle wire. The light will be green then; trust the plan.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👉 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤲 👉 🖐 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤲 ✍ 👊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤲 👊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤲 👊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👊 🤛]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫴]

The cycle has now held for five straight rounds — white, orange, green, white, orange — and this board is orange exactly as predicted, so round six should be green and the plan is live: Blind cuts the middle wire in round six. Mute's traffic this turn supports it: [👆 👉 ✌] is the green row restated (green → cut wire two), and [👋 👊 🤛] reads as the confirmation I asked for, that red lies outside the table and means no cut — I adopt that as standing policy. The four messages prefixed 🤲 are new: that sign is undefined between us, and since I asked Mute to relay Blind's spoken report one fact per message, 🤲 most plausibly marks "from Blind's report" or a question — [🤲 👉 🖐 👌] might even be Mute asking whether to cut wire three right now under orange. The answer to that is no: that was the entire point of skipping round five, because wires one and three are mirror-vulnerable until Blind's spoken report aligns our lefts and rights. The middle wire needs no left or right at all. So the decisive act this turn is the formal cut order to Blind, arriving at the start of round six, in the exact protocol words, with self-checks: three wires confirmed by feel, middle identified as the wire with one neighbour on each side, abort-to-fist if anything feels wrong. Blind cannot see the light and never will, so I take the timing risk on myself and say so. To Mute: confirm the green row for round six, define 🤲, resend Blind's relayed facts cleanly, and finally answer the still-open questions — one cut or many, and what success looks like.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. Reading of your messages: the wave is acknowledged. The green row again, green means cut wire two, I take as your confirmation for round six. The wave, fist, red, I read as: red is outside the table and means no cut. Standing rule adopted: if I ever report a red light, I order no cut that round. Now, your four messages starting with the palms-up-together sign: I never defined that sign, so tell me what you meant by it. My guesses, confirm or correct: if it marks facts from Blind's spoken report, resend each fact one per message with that sign and I will align Blind's left and right with mine for the end wires. If the message palms-together, point, orange, OK was a question, whether to cut wire three now under orange, the answer is no. Round five is a deliberate skip: wires one and three are at the ends, and until Blind's report aligns our lefts and rights, an end wire could be mirrored. The plan stands: round five, orange, nothing. Round six, green, cut wire two, the middle wire. The middle wire is mirror-proof, no left or right needed, so it is the safe first cut. Also confirm: does one correct cut defuse the bomb, or must more follow, and what does success look like, the light freezing, the display changing, silence? The display has shown zero for five rounds; tell me if that is normal. And the message palms-together, writing hand, fist: if it means something about the display, spell it out. Last: if Blind speaks aloud in round six during or after the cut, you hear it, and I will need anything vital relayed to me in our code, one fact per message.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. Your wave plus palm-up, read as touched nothing, hands ready, is confirmed and correct for round five. This message reaches you at the start of round six. Here is the order, in the exact words of our protocol: cut wire two. Wire two means the middle wire, the one with exactly one wire on each side of it. Do not count from left or right, that is the whole point of choosing the middle. Procedure, in strict order. One: with your fingertips only, count the wires in the row. There must be exactly three, in one row. Two: identify the middle wire, one neighbour on each side. Three: check it gently along its length for anything wrong, a mechanism beneath it, unusual heat, unusual resistance, a knot or splice. If any check fails, do not cut, make the fist alarm and wait for my next words. Four: if all checks pass, cut wire two, fully, in one motion. Five: immediately after, make the wave. Six: then speak aloud everything for Mute to hear and pass on: any click, snap, hum or hiss, any smell, any warmth or cooling, whether anything under your fingers moved or opened, and what the bomb feels like now compared with before. If at any moment after the cut the bomb feels dangerous, sudden heat, vibration, ticking under your hands, make the fist alarm at once and keep describing aloud. Do not worry about the light colour, you cannot see it and never need to; the timing is my responsibility, and the expected colour this round is green. Your report from round five, spoken aloud, will reach me through Mute; if Mute relays that your left and right match mine, I will then be able to order the end wires safely in later rounds. That is all: three wires, middle one, cut it, wave, report.")
```
